translationRepairs: His father Berdena had led the entire clan over in submission when the imperial armies swept the Western Regions in the gengchen year (1240).
His father Berdena had led the entire clan over in submission when the imperial armies swept the Western Regions in the gengchen year (1220).
The sexagenary designation and the western-campaign context identify the year as 1220, not 1240; the repair changes only the erroneous supplied Gregorian gloss.
He also ordered the Models for Emperors to be rendered into Mongolian.
He also ordered the Models for Emperors to be translated.
The source says only that the work was translated; it does not specify Mongolian as the target language.

In 1308 he was appointed Grand Preceptor with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and grand councillor for military and state affairs of the first rank, made a Pillar of the State, and continued as Minister of Agriculture and Duke of Ying.

In 1308 he was granted the rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi (with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies), appointed Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and grand councillor for military and state affairs of the first rank, made a Pillar of the State, and retained as Minister of Agriculture and Duke of Ying.
The proposal correctly separates 開府儀同三司 from Grand Preceptor, but it leaves 太子詹事 mistranslated as Grand Mentor. The revision renders the prestige rank and household office distinctly.

In the first year of Zhida (1308) he was appointed Grand Preceptor with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Grand Councillor for Military and State Affairs of the First Rank, and Pillar of the State, while retaining his former posts as Minister of Agriculture and Duke of Ying.

In the first year of Zhida (1308) he was granted the rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi, with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies, and appointed Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and Grand Councillor for Military and State Affairs of the First Rank; he was also made a Pillar of the State while retaining his former posts as Minister of Agriculture and Duke of Ying.
The source lists 開府儀同三司 and 太子詹事 as separate honors or offices. The proposal fixes the former but not the latter, so the literal rendering is revised in both places.

In 1311 he was appointed Grand Mentor, recorder of military and state affairs of the first rank, and grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, while continuing as Minister of Agriculture and overseeing the Chongxiang Court and the Directorate of Astronomy; his other offices, honors, and enfeoffment were unchanged.

In 1311 he was appointed Grand Guardian, recorder of military and state affairs of the first rank, and grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, while continuing as Minister of Agriculture and overseeing the Chongxiang Court and the Directorate of Astronomy; his other offices, honors, and enfeoffment were unchanged.
太保 is Grand Guardian; Grand Mentor would translate 太傅.

In the fourth year (1311) he was appointed Grand Mentor, Recorder of Military and State Affairs of the First Rank, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, while also serving as Minister of Agriculture and overseeing the Chongxiang Court and the Directorate of Astronomy; his offices, titles, honors, and enfeoffment remained as before.

In the fourth year (1311) he was appointed Grand Guardian, Recorder of Military and State Affairs of the First Rank, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, while also serving as Minister of Agriculture and overseeing the Chongxiang Court and the Directorate of Astronomy; his offices, titles, honors, and enfeoffment remained as before.
The literal field makes the same 太保/太傅 error, and the proposed title correction is exact.
When Chengzong died, the powerful minister A Bu controlled the inner palace and sent no envoys to announce the mourning to the imperial princes.
When Chengzong died, powerful ministers curried favor with the empress's palace and sent no envoys to announce the mourning to the imperial princes.
阿附 is a verb meaning to attach oneself or curry favor, not the name A Bu. 中宮 here denotes the empress's palace; the proposed 'attached themselves' is accurate but stiff English.
When Chengzong died, the powerful minister A Bu controlled the inner palace and did not send envoys to announce the mourning to the imperial princes.
When Chengzong died, powerful ministers attached themselves to the empress's palace and did not send envoys to announce the mourning to the imperial princes.
The literal rendering must parse 阿附 as the predicate and 中宮 as its object rather than inventing a minister named A Bu.
The Prince of Huaining and Your Highness are worthy grandsons of Taizu and Yu Huang; the hearts of the people have long belonged to you.
The Prince of Huaining and Your Highness are worthy descendants of Shizu and Emperor Yuzong; the hearts of the people have long belonged to you.
世祖 is Shizu, not Taizu, and 裕皇 refers to Emperor Yuzong. 'Descendants' conveys 孫 without imposing a single generation on both antecedents.
Yet he kept his counsel discreet and never let resentment show abroad.
Yet he kept a low profile, shunned self-importance, and disclosed nothing outside the palace.
韜晦惡盈 describes deliberate self-effacement and aversion to overreaching, not concealed resentment. The proposal catches the semantic error but is not polished English.
The following year he entered service as master of the heir's household and was advanced to Grand Master of Proper Service.
The following year he entered service as master of the heir's household and was advanced to Grand Master for Proper Attendance.
正奉大夫 is a distinct rank from 中奉大夫 in the preceding appointment, so reusing 'Proper Service' would erase a real distinction.
The following year he entered service as Master of the Heir Apparent's Household and was advanced to Grand Master of Proper Service.
The following year he entered service as Master of the Heir Apparent's Household and was advanced to Grand Master for Proper Attendance.
The literal field should likewise preserve the distinction between 中奉大夫 and 正奉大夫.
If you and I and all the armies exert ourselves in loyal service to the throne, nothing should fail."
If the armies and I each devote ourselves loyally to the royal cause, there is nothing we should not accomplish."

吾與諸軍 means the speaker and the armies, not 'you and I.' The revision removes the invented addressee, improves the proposal's grammar, and preserves the closing quotation mark required by the source unit.
In all there were two hundred thousand shi of grain, as much again in beans, five hundred fifty thousand sets of arms and armor, and fodder by the ten thousand bundles.
In all there were two hundred thousand shi of grain, as much again in beans, five hundred fifty thousand sets of arms and armor, and fodder numbering one hundred million.
萬萬 is one hundred million, not ten thousand. The proposed 'myriad myriads' conveys the arithmetic but is unsuitable for polished idiomatic English; the source supplies no unit for the fodder count.
In all there were two hundred thousand shi of grain, the same amount of beans, five hundred fifty thousand sets of armor and weapons, and ten thousand bundles of fodder.
In all there were two hundred thousand shi of grain, the same amount of beans, five hundred fifty thousand sets of armor and weapons, and fodder numbering one hundred million.
The literal field must preserve the full value of 萬萬. 'One hundred million' is exact and clearer than the proposed calque 'a myriad myriads.'

Surveillance Commissioner Dong Shouzhong and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Shasha were at Nanyang; Right Vice Councillor Tuotiemuer and Surveillance Commissioner Buyan were at Hulao; troops and horses were dispatched separately to await his orders.

Surveillance Commissioner Dong Shouzhong and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Shasha were at Nanyang; Right Vice Councillor Tuotiemuer and Surveillance Commissioner Buyan were at Hulao; troops and horses were dispatched separately for their use.
其 refers collectively to the officials just listed, and 聽其調用 means that the forces were placed at their disposal. The proposal's 'await their deployment' is less direct.

The westerners still beat and robbed Lanzhu and interrogated him to learn the truth, while the court also sent Chief Guardian Yelü Timur with more than ten followers bearing an edict to disband the western army at Hulao.

The westerners still beat and robbed Lanzhu and interrogated him to learn the truth, while the court also sent Chief Guardian Yuelü Timur with more than ten followers bearing an edict to disband the western army at Hulao.
月魯 is not the Khitan surname 耶律. Yuelü preserves the source's distinct transcription and avoids the false identification created by Yelü.

The westerners still beat and plundered Lanzhu and interrogated him for the truth, while the court also dispatched the Chief Guardian Yelü Timur with more than ten followers bearing an edict to disband the western army at Hulao.

The westerners still beat and plundered Lanzhu and interrogated him for the truth, while the court also dispatched the Chief Guardian Yuelü Timur with more than ten followers bearing an edict to disband the western army at Hulao.
The same name correction is required in the literal field: 月魯帖木兒 cannot be represented as the surname Yelü.
Later, for his service he was made grand censor of the Shaanxi branch secretariat and again appointed grand councillor of the Central Secretariat.
Later, for his service he was made grand censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate and again appointed grand councillor of the Central Secretariat.
行御史 identifies a branch censorate, whereas a branch secretariat would be 行中書省 or 行省. The proposed correction is exact.
In the eighth year of Dade (1304) a general amnesty was proclaimed; at court it was debated that only officials who had accepted bribes in the course of affairs would not participate.
In the eighth year of Dade (1304), a general amnesty was proclaimed; at court it was proposed that only officials who had accepted bribes in the course of official business be excluded.
不預 means exclusion from the amnesty, not voluntary nonparticipation. The revision also preserves 惟, which limits the proposed exclusion to this class of officials.
At the opening of the Zhida reign a Ministry of Revenue was established; he was appointed associate minister of revenue affairs and summoned to the capital, but firmly declined.
At the opening of the Zhida reign a Department of State Affairs was established; he was appointed counsellor of the Department of State Affairs and summoned to the capital, but firmly declined.
尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs, not the Ministry of Revenue, and 參議尚書省事 is a counsellorship in that department.
At the beginning of the Zhida reign the Ministry of Revenue was established; he was appointed associate minister of revenue affairs, summoned to the capital, and earnestly declined to accept.

At the beginning of the Zhida reign the Department of State Affairs was established; he was appointed counsellor of the Department of State Affairs, summoned to the capital, and earnestly declined to accept.
The literal field contains the same institutional error; the proposed Department of State Affairs terminology matches 尚書省 and its counsellor.
